---
title: "What's new in lactater 1.0"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(lactater)
plex <- requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE) &&
  isTRUE(suppressMessages(systemfonts::require_font("IBM Plex Sans", fallback = "sans")))
if (plex) options(lactater.font = "IBM Plex Sans")
```

lactater 1.0 follows each method's original paper, solves every threshold exactly, and adds plots that explain
themselves, tools to compare tests and measure training load, and real example data. Because the methods are now
computed as their authors defined them, some thresholds differ from version 0.3.0. This page shows by how much on
`demo_data` (with the resting sample included in the fit), and why.

## How the numbers compare with 0.3.0

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(lactater)
library(dplyr)

old <- tibble(
  method = c("Log-log", "OBLA 2.0", "OBLA 2.5", "OBLA 3.0", "OBLA 3.5", "OBLA 4.0",
             "Bsln + 0.5", "Bsln + 1.0", "Bsln + 1.5", "Dmax", "ModDmax", "Exp-Dmax",
             "Log-Poly-ModDmax", "Log-Exp-ModDmax", "LTP1", "LTP2", "LTratio"),
  version_0.3.0 = c(83.4, 105.4, 118.5, 129.0, 137.0, 145.0, 82.5, 103.6, 116.7,
                    131.5, 140.1, 134.8, 143.0, 145.7, 88.8, 147.6, 71.2)
)
new <- lactate_threshold(demo_data, intensity, lactate, include_baseline = TRUE, plot = FALSE)
## the unrounded intensities, to compare at 0.1 W
unrounded <- attr(new, "lactater")$intensity
old |>
  inner_join(tibble(method = names(unrounded), version_1.0 = round(unname(unrounded), 1)), by = "method") |>
  mutate(difference = version_1.0 - version_0.3.0)
```

## Why they differ

* **OBLA and Bsln+ (about +1 to +2 W).** The intensity at a target lactate is solved on the fitted curve itself
  (issue #8, thanks to Simon Dierickx).
* **D<sub>max</sub> family.** Each variant takes the point where the fitted curve lies furthest below its line, so a curve that
  levels off at the end (a last-stage plateau, or sweat lactate) gets a sensible D<sub>max</sub> at any lactate scale. The
  line runs from its start to the last stage, and its ends sit where each paper put them: on the curve for D<sub>max</sub> and
  Exp-D<sub>max</sub>, at the measured values for ModD<sub>max</sub> and at the last stage of the Log-log variants (`dmax_anchor` changes
  this). The Log-log start is computed without the resting sample, as documented.
* **Log-log.** Two separate straight lines that share the stage between them, as in [Beaver et al. (1985)](https://doi.org/10.1152/jappl.1985.59.6.1936), split at
  the stage with the lowest residual sum of squares; the threshold is where they cross.
* **LTP.** The turn points are the exact least-squares optimum on the measured stages, found by exhaustive search,
  so they never depend on starting values.
* **LTratio.** The exact minimum, within the exercise stages.
* **Heart rate.** Interpolated between the measured stages, so it follows the bend of the heart-rate curve.
* **Resting sample.** It is the row with intensity 0, so tests without one keep all their stages.

## New in 1.0

* Plots that show how each method works, a forest-style overview of every threshold with a table of values, and
  night and journal styles.
* IAT, flexible targets (`fixed`, `baseline_plus`, `iat_rise`), and one turn point for submaximal tests
  (`ltp_breakpoints = 1`).
* Confidence intervals (`ci = TRUE`), `lactate_checks()`, `lactate_diagnostics()`, `lactate_fit_quality()` and
  `lactate_report()`.
* RPE (6-20 and CR10) at each threshold and in the zones.
* `lactate_zones()` (three or five zones) and `training_load()`: time in zone and intensity distribution.
* `compare_tests()`, `curve_shift()`, `curve_shape()`, `lactate_trend()` and `relative_thresholds()` to compare tests
  and athletes.
* `lactate_tests`: 15 real and simulated tests across sports and fitness levels.
* Rowing, grouped analysis (`.by`), and `vlamax()`.

See the [news](../news/index.html) for the full list.
